subject.title: policy: repair denied gateway http endpoints

question: Should `policy/gateway-http-endpoint-enabled` be accepted as an automatic `doctor --fix` repair that disables reported Gateway HTTP endpoint `enabled` leaves when `workspaceRepairs=true`?
rationale: The patch is narrow and proven, but it intentionally converts a review-required Gateway HTTP policy finding into an automatic config mutation affecting existing workspaces that opted into policy repairs.

options.title: Accept Automatic Endpoint Repair
options.body: Land the PR with maintainer-owned compatibility and security-boundary risk because it only narrows reported endpoint `enabled` leaves and preserves nested endpoint config.

options.title: Keep Review-Required
options.body: Decline the automatic mutation and leave the finding review-required if maintainers want endpoint disabling to remain a manual policy action.

options.title: Ask For Packaged CLI Smoke
options.body: Require one packaged or dev CLI `doctor --fix` smoke before merge if maintainers want stronger end-to-end proof than the source-entry repair transcript.

recommendation.title: Accept Automatic Endpoint Repair
recommendation.body: Land the PR with maintainer-owned compatibility and security-boundary risk because it only narrows reported endpoint `enabled` leaves and preserves nested endpoint config.

likelyOwner.reason: They carried the adjacent Policy doctor repair stack and best know the intended automatic-repair boundary, though final acceptance still needs maintainer authority because of the protected label.
